lessons.title: Aston Villa’s origins
lessons.subtitle: Follow a local idea as it grew into a football institution.

story.title: A football club takes shape
story.body: Four members of Aston Villa Wesleyan Chapel’s Male Adult Bible Class chose association football in 1874. They had considered rugby after watching a colleague play, but decided it was too physical.

story.title: A league-making club
story.body: Villa committee member William McGregor proposed a structured home-and-away competition to leading clubs. The Football League was formed in 1888, and Villa finished second in its first season.

facts.label: Villa’s founding year
facts.prompt: In what year does Aston Villa trace its formation?
facts.scope: Aston Villa’s formation, as dated in the club timeline.
facts.evidence: The club timeline dates the four founders’ decision to create a football club to 1874.

facts.label: Villa’s Football League organizer
facts.prompt: Which Aston Villa committee member proposed a home-and-away league to other clubs?
facts.scope: The Football League’s formation in 1888.
facts.evidence: Aston Villa’s history credits committee member William McGregor with writing to other clubs to propose organized home-and-away fixtures.

facts.label: Villa’s first league title
facts.prompt: In which year did Aston Villa secure its first League title?
facts.scope: Aston Villa’s club history.
facts.evidence: The club timeline states its first League title was secured in 1894.

lessons.title: A Wembley final remembered
lessons.subtitle: A cup final turned on a pair of goals.

story.title: Underdogs at Wembley
story.body: Aston Villa met Matt Busby’s Manchester United in the 1957 FA Cup Final, played at Wembley on 4 May. United were chasing the Double.

story.title: McParland makes history
story.body: Peter McParland headed Villa ahead in the 68th minute, then scored again five minutes later. Villa held on for their seventh FA Cup and first major trophy in about 37 years.

facts.label: 1957 FA Cup final date
facts.prompt: On what date was Aston Villa’s 1957 FA Cup Final against Manchester United played?
facts.scope: Aston Villa–Manchester United, 1957 FA Cup Final.
facts.evidence: The club timeline dates the Wembley final to 4 May 1957.

facts.label: 1957 final opponent
facts.prompt: Who did Aston Villa face in the 1957 FA Cup Final?
facts.scope: Aston Villa’s 1957 FA Cup Final.
facts.evidence: The club’s final account identifies Matt Busby’s Manchester United as Villa’s opponent.

facts.label: McParland’s final goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Peter McParland score for Aston Villa in the 1957 FA Cup Final?
facts.scope: Peter McParland’s scoring in the 1957 FA Cup Final.
facts.evidence: The club timeline describes McParland’s 68th-minute header and his second goal five minutes later.

lessons.title: A night in Rotterdam
lessons.subtitle: One substitution changed the shape of a European final.

story.title: A sudden change in goal
story.body: Aston Villa played Bayern Munich at Rotterdam’s De Kuip on 26 May 1982. Jimmy Rimmer was injured after nine minutes, and Nigel Spink came on for only his second senior Villa appearance.

story.title: One decisive finish
story.body: Tony Morley’s cross found Peter Withe, who scored in the 67th minute. Villa won the European Cup final 1–0 and captain Dennis Mortimer lifted the trophy.

facts.label: European Cup final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Aston Villa play Bayern Munich in the European Cup final?
facts.scope: 1981/82 European Cup Final, played at De Kuip in Rotterdam.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s official finals publication lists the Aston Villa–Bayern final on 26 May 1982.

facts.label: European Cup final score
facts.prompt: What was the score in the 1982 European Cup Final, with Aston Villa listed first?
facts.scope: 1982 European Cup final; Aston Villa listed before Bayern München.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s official final record lists Aston Villa 1–0 Bayern München.

facts.label: Withe’s winning-goal minute
facts.prompt: In which minute did Peter Withe score Aston Villa’s winning goal in the 1982 European Cup Final?
facts.scope: Peter Withe’s goal for Aston Villa against Bayern Munich in the 1982 European Cup Final.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s official final line-up and results record credits Withe with the 67th-minute goal.

lessons.title: From Ireland to England
lessons.subtitle: An evolving path across several club chapters.

story.title: From Dalkey to Inchicore
story.body: St Patrick’s Athletic says it signed McGrath from Dalkey United in 1981. The club first considered him as a centre-forward, then recognized his ability at centre-half.

story.title: A move to England
story.body: St Pat’s records that McGrath transferred to Manchester United after the 1981–82 season and later moved on to Aston Villa. Derby County dates his arrival from Villa to October 1996.

facts.label: McGrath’s first senior club
facts.prompt: Which Dublin club signed Paul McGrath from Dalkey United in 1981?
facts.scope: Paul McGrath’s move from Dalkey United in 1981.
facts.evidence: St Patrick’s Athletic states that it signed McGrath from Dalkey United in summer 1981.

facts.label: McGrath’s 1982 destination
facts.prompt: Which English club did McGrath join after the 1981–82 season?
facts.scope: Paul McGrath’s transfer from St Patrick’s Athletic after the 1981–82 season.
facts.evidence: The St Pat’s profile says he was transferred to Manchester United at the end of 1981–82.

facts.label: McGrath’s Derby move
facts.prompt: In what month and year did Derby County say McGrath arrived from Aston Villa?
facts.scope: Paul McGrath’s transfer from Aston Villa to Derby County.
facts.evidence: Derby County states he arrived from Aston Villa in October 1996.

lessons.title: Recognition across a career
lessons.subtitle: Club and international chapters brought lasting recognition.

story.title: An early individual award
story.body: St Patrick’s Athletic records McGrath as the 1981–82 PFAI Player of the Year. The award came during his season at Richmond Park before his move to Manchester United.

story.title: An international legacy
story.body: The club’s report, published in August 2020, credits McGrath with 83 senior caps and describes his Hall of Fame recognition as part of the 2019 FAI International Awards edition.

facts.label: McGrath’s first major individual honour
facts.prompt: Which PFAI award did McGrath win in 1981–82?
distractors: PFAI Young Player of the Year
FAI International Player of the Year
facts.scope: Paul McGrath’s 1981–82 season with St Patrick’s Athletic.
facts.evidence: St Patrick’s Athletic calls him the winner of the second-ever PFAI Player of the Year award in 1981–82.

facts.label: McGrath’s Ireland total
facts.prompt: How many senior caps does the FAI Hall of Fame announcement credit to McGrath?
facts.scope: Paul McGrath’s senior appearances for Ireland.
facts.evidence: The FAI Hall of Fame announcement states that McGrath won 83 senior caps.

facts.label: A national honour
facts.prompt: Which association honoured Paul McGrath with a Hall of Fame award in its 2019 awards edition?
facts.scope: Paul McGrath: 2019 FAI International Awards edition, reported on 8 August 2020.
facts.evidence: The club article dated 8 August 2020 describes McGrath receiving the Hall of Fame award as part of the 2019 Three FAI International Awards; it does not establish a 2019 presentation date.

lessons.title: A World Cup defensive display
lessons.subtitle: FIFA’s match account shows the work behind a landmark result.

story.title: A landmark result
story.body: Ireland beat Italy 1–0 in their 1994 World Cup group match. Ray Houghton scored the only goal in the 11th minute.

story.title: A defensive masterclass
story.body: FIFA’s match retrospective credits McGrath with 15 headers won, six clearances, five interceptions, three blocks, and two tackles as he marked Roberto Baggio and Italy.

facts.label: Ireland’s 1994 World Cup result
facts.prompt: What was the score in the 1994 World Cup match, with Ireland listed first and Italy second?
facts.scope: Republic of Ireland–Italy, 1994 FIFA World Cup group match; teams stated Ireland first.
facts.evidence: FIFA’s retrospective states Ireland beat Italy 1–0.

facts.label: McGrath’s headers won
facts.prompt: How many headers does FIFA credit McGrath with winning against Italy in 1994?
facts.scope: Paul McGrath’s defensive work in Ireland’s 1–0 win over Italy at USA 1994.
facts.evidence: FIFA lists 15 headers won in McGrath’s match performance.

facts.label: McGrath’s interceptions
facts.prompt: How many interceptions does FIFA list for McGrath against Italy?
facts.scope: Paul McGrath’s defensive statistics in Ireland–Italy at USA 1994.
facts.evidence: FIFA lists five interceptions among McGrath’s defensive actions.

lessons.title: A World Cup quarter-final
lessons.subtitle: A tournament run reached a defining knockout match.

story.title: A place in the last eight
story.body: UEFA’s match account lists McGrath in Ireland’s starting line-up for the 1990 World Cup quarter-final against Italy. The match was Ireland’s first appearance in a major-tournament quarter-final.

story.title: A narrow result
story.body: Salvatore Schillaci scored the only goal in Rome. Italy advanced after a 1–0 win over Ireland.

facts.label: McGrath at Italia 90
facts.prompt: In which year did McGrath start Ireland’s World Cup quarter-final against Italy?
facts.scope: Paul McGrath’s appearance in Ireland’s 1990 FIFA World Cup quarter-final.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s match line-up for Italy–Ireland lists McGrath in the Ireland starting XI.

facts.label: Ireland’s tournament run
facts.prompt: At what stage did Ireland meet Italy at the 1990 World Cup?
facts.scope: Italy–Ireland at Italia 90.
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies the match as the 1990 World Cup quarter-final.

facts.label: The match’s only goal
facts.prompt: Who scored the only goal in Italy’s 1–0 quarter-final win over Ireland?
facts.scope: Italy–Ireland, 1990 FIFA World Cup quarter-final.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s match account records Schillaci scoring in the 38th minute.

lessons.title: A rise through the ranks
lessons.subtitle: Villa performances led to a new chapter at Old Trafford.

story.title: A high-profile move
story.body: The Premier League records Yorke arriving at Manchester United from Aston Villa in August 1998. The transfer came after a prolific run at Villa Park.

story.title: A productive Villa spell
story.body: The Premier League season record shows 17 Villa goals in 1995/96. Aston Villa later noted that Yorke reached at least 15 league goal involvements in three successive seasons from 1995/96 through 1997/98.

facts.label: Yorke’s next club
facts.prompt: Which club signed Yorke from Aston Villa in 1998?
facts.scope: Dwight Yorke’s 1998 transfer from Aston Villa.
facts.evidence: The Premier League states that Yorke arrived at Manchester United from Aston Villa in August 1998.

facts.label: A prolific league season
facts.prompt: How many Premier League goals did Yorke score for Aston Villa in 1995/96?
facts.scope: Dwight Yorke’s Aston Villa Premier League record for 1995/96.
facts.evidence: The Premier League player profile’s season table lists 17 goals for Yorke in 1995/96.

facts.label: A sustained run of form
facts.prompt: Across how many consecutive seasons did Yorke reach 15 or more Premier League goal involvements for Villa, according to the club?
facts.scope: Yorke’s Premier League goal involvements from 1995/96 through 1997/98.
facts.evidence: Aston Villa identifies Yorke among the players with 15+ involvements in each of three consecutive seasons, 1995/96 to 1997/98.

lessons.title: A Wembley afternoon
lessons.subtitle: A cup final gave Yorke a memorable moment.

story.title: A final against Leeds
story.body: The EFL’s official finals record lists Aston Villa’s 3–0 win over Leeds United in the 1996 League Cup final. It names Dwight Yorke as the scorer of Villa’s third goal in the 88th minute.

story.title: A personal contribution
story.body: Yorke’s late goal completed the scoring at Wembley. The EFL record confirms his part in the final rather than only the club’s trophy result.

facts.label: The final result
facts.prompt: What was the score in the 1996 League Cup final, with Aston Villa listed first?
facts.scope: 1996 League Cup final; Aston Villa listed before Leeds United.
facts.evidence: The EFL finals record gives Aston Villa 3–0 Leeds United.

facts.label: Yorke’s Wembley goal
facts.prompt: In which minute did Yorke score Villa’s third goal in the 1996 League Cup final?
facts.scope: Dwight Yorke’s goal in Aston Villa–Leeds United, 1996 League Cup final.
facts.evidence: The EFL finals record lists Dwight Yorke as Villa’s scorer in the 88th minute.

facts.label: The Wembley honour
facts.prompt: Which competition’s final did Aston Villa win against Leeds United in 1996?
facts.scope: Aston Villa’s 1996 final against Leeds United.
facts.evidence: The EFL page identifies the match as the 1996 League Cup final.

lessons.title: A high-profile transfer
lessons.subtitle: A new chapter began with an extraordinary first season.

story.title: A move to Old Trafford
story.body: Yorke joined United from Aston Villa in August 1998. His first season brought 29 goals in all competitions and an 18-goal Premier League campaign.

story.title: A huge first season
story.body: The Premier League reports 29 goals in all competitions during Yorke’s first United season. Its Golden Boot table lists his 18 league goals alongside joint winners Michael Owen and Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink. UEFA lists Yorke and Andriy Shevchenko as joint Champions League top scorers with eight goals each.

facts.label: Yorke’s treble-season total
facts.prompt: How many goals does the Premier League credit Yorke with scoring in all competitions after joining United in 1998?
facts.scope: Dwight Yorke’s first Manchester United season, 1998/99; all competitions.
facts.evidence: The Premier League says Yorke scored 29 times after arriving from Villa in August 1998.

facts.label: Yorke’s league scoring honour
facts.prompt: How many Premier League goals did Yorke score in United’s 1998/99 campaign?
facts.scope: Dwight Yorke’s Manchester United Premier League campaign in 1998/99.
facts.evidence: The Premier League’s winners table lists Yorke, Owen and Hasselbaink jointly on 18 goals for 1998/99.

facts.label: Yorke’s European scoring
facts.prompt: How many Champions League goals did Dwight Yorke score in United’s 1998/99 winning campaign?
facts.scope: Dwight Yorke’s 1998/99 UEFA Champions League campaign for Manchester United.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s 1998/99 season overview lists Yorke and Shevchenko as joint top scorers with eight goals each.

lessons.title: On football’s biggest stage
lessons.subtitle: A national team made history in Germany.

story.title: A historic qualification
story.body: Trinidad and Tobago made its first FIFA World Cup appearance at Germany 2006. FIFA’s retrospective describes the tournament as the country’s only World Cup appearance at the time.

story.title: Captain on the world stage
story.body: FIFA identifies Yorke as Trinidad and Tobago captain. The team opened with a goalless draw against Sweden before meeting England and Paraguay.

facts.label: Yorke’s national team
facts.prompt: Which country did Dwight Yorke captain at the 2006 FIFA World Cup?
facts.scope: Dwight Yorke’s captaincy at Germany 2006.
facts.evidence: FIFA’s official tournament collectible identifies Yorke as Trinidad and Tobago’s captain.

facts.label: T&T’s World Cup debut
facts.prompt: In which year did Trinidad and Tobago make its first FIFA World Cup appearance?
facts.scope: Trinidad and Tobago’s first FIFA World Cup appearance, captained by Yorke.
facts.evidence: FIFA says the country’s only World Cup appearance came at Germany 2006.

facts.label: T&T’s opening match
facts.prompt: What was the result of Trinidad and Tobago’s opening match against Sweden at the 2006 World Cup?
facts.scope: Trinidad and Tobago–Sweden, 2006 FIFA World Cup group stage.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s final-draw facts, page 42, list Sweden’s 2006 World Cup group results: Trinidad and Tobago 0–0, Paraguay 1–0, England 2–2.
